## 2

I understand why some images or institutions might make you skeptical, but the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on trusting space agencies or photographs. People have measured Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, observed ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, tracked different stars from different latitudes, and circumnavigated the planet. Satellites, GPS, time zones, and long-distance flight routes also work because Earth is approximately spherical. These are observations made by many independent people and organizations, not just one source.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors mixed together. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

That’s also why sunsets often look red or orange. When the Sun is low, its light travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before the light reaches us, leaving more red and orange light.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕开，昏黄的光铺在湿漉漉的路面上，映出摇晃的树影。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，轮胎划开积水，声音很快又被雨幕吞没。屋檐下，一只流浪猫蜷缩着躲雨，眼睛在黑暗中微微发亮。屋里没有人说话，只有钟表的滴答声和窗外连绵不断的雨声，陪着夜色慢慢变深。
